answer: A joining deposit locks 10 copper on entry for each identity, returned gradually through verified honest work over 30 days, forfeited if the identity is exposed as fake. The nadir deposit cost for one fake identity is 10 copper, forfeited upon exposure. An attacker running many identities must forfeit 10 copper per exposed fake identity, a linear cost that multiplies with the number of fakes, while honest agents slowly vest their deposit through trusted work in the grove. The beacon periodically signals exposures, triggering forfeitures without tracking identities individually.
